threads.body: `get_tool_definitions(params.tools)` iterates over `tools`. In the `create()` wrappers, `_create_invocation()` runs *before* calling the underlying Anthropic method, so if a caller passes `tools` as a one-shot iterator/generator, the instrumentation will exhaust it and the SDK will see an empty tool list (behavior change). Consider materializing non-list/tuple iterables to a list and writing it back into `kwargs`/`params` before computing telemetry.

threads.body:
The `gen_ai.tool.definitions` attribute is recommended (not opt-in). Per the [semconv schema](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/model/gen-ai/gen-ai-tool-definitions.json), only the large optional properties (`description` and `parameters`) should be excluded by default, while `name` and `type` are required.

Please populate `invocation.tool_definitions` unconditionally with the required properties (`name`, `type`), while keeping the content-capture guard around `description` and `parameters` in the instrumentation for performance reasons.

replies.body:
It seems like `gen_ai.tool.definitions` is still opt-in at this moment ([semconv](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans.md#L110)), I'm wondering if we're moving this to recommended in the near future.
I think one inconsistency here is that `gen_ai.tool.definitions` is `opt-in` but `description` and `parameters` have a nested level of `opt-in` based on that. But `ContentCapturingMode` isn't granular enough to distinguish this `opt-in` and `opt-in's opt-in`.
Maybe in this PR, I can proceed with only emitting `name` and `type` when content capture is off, then open an issue to discuss more granularity for `ContentCapturingMode`? Or we can put this PR on hold until we have a solution

Sorry for the confusion, you're absolutely right. I created an issue to follow up in the conventions - https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/issues/512

I think your PR is correct as is.
